goal: Deliver a provider-neutral production readiness baseline for the Control Plane and PostgreSQL runtime without adding cloud-specific deployment or first-party identity.
completed: Created codex/p2-production-readiness stacked from P1 commit e024603 while P1 PR #10 remains open.
Added centralized Control Plane runtime configuration with production fail-closed token/origin policy, bounded timeouts, version reporting, audit sink configuration, and database pool validation.
Added GET /ready readiness probe with safe 503 responses for unavailable or incomplete PostgreSQL state; retained GET /health as liveness.
Refactored Control Plane server startup into create/start interfaces with structured request/error logging, request ids, redaction, HTTP timeouts, graceful shutdown, SSE drain, and pool close.
Added shared migration contract and database readiness adapter used by db:check and /ready; migrations remain explicit and are not run automatically by the server.
Added local-skippable/CI-required PostgreSQL contract runner and GitHub Actions PostgreSQL 16 service job.
Updated OpenAPI, README, security/persistence docs, production runbook, observability guidance, architecture module docs, repo map, and business graph metadata.
decisions: Use one gpt-5.6-sol high-reasoning coding agent; shared server, security, persistence, CI, and documentation contracts make parallel agents more likely to drift.
Keep Bearer token application security and delegate TLS, OIDC/RBAC, cookie CSRF, rate limiting, secret rotation, and durable audit shipping to the edge/deployment platform.
Keep /health as liveness and add /ready as readiness; probes remain unauthenticated for orchestration but still observe the origin allowlist when an Origin header is supplied.
Use GitHub Actions as canonical CI with an Ubuntu PostgreSQL 16 service; keep filesystem fallback and Windows harness validation.
Do not add a database migration, auto-migrate on startup, cloud deployment, container image, or automatic release behavior in P2.
remaining: Run the forced PostgreSQL integration gate in GitHub Actions after push; local Docker daemon and psql are unavailable.
After P1 PR #10 merges, align/rebase this stacked branch onto the merged main before opening the P2 PR.
Commit/push/PR creation is intentionally not performed in this implementation turn.
risks: GitNexus impact for getPool is CRITICAL: 18 impacted symbols, 9 execution processes, and 3 modules; existing persistence tests and the new real-PostgreSQL suite cover the compatibility surface.
PostgreSQL CI uses a service container only on Ubuntu; Windows continues to validate the cross-platform harness without a local database service.
P1 PR #10 is still open, so the current P2 branch includes P1 as its parent until the branch is aligned after merge.
